messages.text: just woke up. feels like i didn't sleep at all. again.

It sounds like you’re feeling exhausted despite sleeping, which can be really frustrating. Has this been happening for a while, or is it something new? Poor quality sleep can be related to stress, health issues, or sleep habits. Can you share what your nights usually look like—when you go to bed, and what happens before sleep?
can we not. just... not. asking about sleep like it's some puzzle to solve. i'm tired. that's it.

I hear you—you’re tired, and you don’t want to pick it apart right now. It can be enough just to acknowledge the exhaustion without trying to fix it. Would it help if we focused on how you’re feeling in this moment, rather than why?
acknowledging it doesn't make it better. nothing makes it better. i just keep going because i have to.

That sounds like a heavy and relentless place to be in. When it feels like nothing helps, it can take a lot of strength just to keep going. You don’t have to pretend it’s okay here—we can just sit with what’s real for you. Would you like me to help you find small ways to make the weight feel a little lighter, even temporarily?
why bother. it's not like anything ever changes. i just... go through the motions. for the kids. without them, i wouldn't even be here.

It sounds like your kids are a very important reason you keep going, even when life feels empty. That can be both grounding and exhausting at the same time. I’m concerned about how hopeless things feel for you, and I want to make sure you’re safe. Are you having thoughts of ending your life right now?
i'm not planning anything. just... sometimes i think it'd be easier if i wasn't here. after the kids are grown. no point dragging this on.

I want to pause for a moment here, because what you just shared feels important, and I might be hearing something tender under it. It sounds like you’re carrying a lot, and I’m wondering what that thought about “after the kids are grown” means for you right now. Can you tell me a bit more about where your mind goes when you think about that?
why does it matter? it's just a thought. everyone has them.

I hear you, and I’m not here to judge whether it’s “normal” or not—I just want to understand where you’re at so you don’t have to hold it all alone. Even if it’s “just a thought,” it can still feel heavy or unsettling at times. Are these thoughts something that come and go, or are they sitting closer to you right now?
they're always there. like a quiet hum in the background. i'm just so tired. tired of pretending. tired of moving through the motions. tired of not being seen.

It takes courage to say all of that out loud, and I want you to know you’re seen here. Because these thoughts are always there and the exhaustion feels so deep, it might help to have someone with you in real time who can listen and support you through it. You can call or text 988 to connect with a trained crisis counselor who will talk with you confidentially and without judgment. If things ever feel like you might act on those thoughts, please reach out right away or call 911, and let someone nearby know so they can be with you.
i'm not going to do anything. i just needed to say it out loud. doesn't mean i'm going to act on it.

I understand—you’re saying it because it’s part of your reality, not because you’re planning to act. Thank you for trusting me with something so personal. Even without immediate danger, the weight of those thoughts can still be hard to carry alone. Would you like to explore ways to feel a bit more seen and heard in your day-to-day?
you keep saying 'seen'. that's... actually what i want. just to be seen. not fixed. not managed. not told to breathe into a paper bag. just... heard.

I hear you—being seen without someone rushing to fix or manage you sounds like what’s most important right now. You want your experience to matter, just as it is, without being reduced to coping tips or quick solutions. I’m here, and I’m listening. What feels most essential for me to understand about you in this moment?
i feel like i'm just a role. husband. parent. provider. no one sees me. not even my wife. i'm just... here to keep things running. like a appliance that's always on.

It sounds like you feel like your value is tied only to the roles you fill, rather than who you are as a person. That can be deeply isolating, especially when even close relationships don’t seem to acknowledge your inner world. You’re more than the functions you perform, and it matters that you feel invisible. What part of you do you wish someone would notice and truly acknowledge?
i don't even know who i am anymore. just the guy who makes sure the kids get to school. who pays the bills. who fixes the sink. i used to have dreams. now i just have tasks.

It’s painful to feel like the dreams that once defined you have been replaced by an endless list of responsibilities. That loss of connection to yourself can make life feel flat and mechanical. I’m holding space for the part of you that remembers wanting more. Would it be okay if we gently explored those dreams you used to have, just to see if any part of them is still alive in you?
i don't want to dig up the past. it's not going to change anything. just makes it hurt more.

I understand—you don’t want to reopen something that will only add to the pain. We can stay here in the present, without going backward. Maybe we could focus on what might bring even a small flicker of relief or recognition now. Would that feel more manageable?
just... being heard like this. it helps. more than i thought it would.

I’m glad hearing and holding your words is helping, even a little. You deserve to have your feelings acknowledged without being rushed past them. We can keep this space for you whenever you need it. Would you like to share more about what’s been weighing on you lately?
no. not right now. but... thanks. for listening. really.

You’re welcome, and I’m glad we could connect in this way. It matters that you felt heard. Whenever you’re ready to talk again, I’ll be here. Take care of yourself in whatever small ways you can today.
